{{nihongo|'''Shimaana Shrine'''|島穴神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kazusa Province]].

=== Enshrined deities ===
The following three deities are enshrined.
; Main enshrined deity
:* '''{{ill|Shinatsuhiko|Q1073925|qid=Q1073925|lt=Shinatsuhiko-no-Mikoto}}''' (しなつひこのみこと) - a wind deity. In shrine tradition, this deity is regarded as the husband or younger brother of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shinatobe-no-Mikoto}}, the enshrined deity of {{ill|Anesaki Shrine|ja|姉埼神社|sv|Anesaki-jinja|qid=Q11447235}}.
; Associated deities
:* {{ill|Kuma District, Kumamoto|ceb|Kuma-gun|fr|District de Kuma|it|Distretto di Kuma|ja|球磨郡|ko|구마군|lt|Kumos apskritis|pl|Powiat Kuma|zh|球磨郡|qid=Q1132476|lt=Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto}} (やまとたけるのみこと)
:* {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Q4388732|qid=Q4388732|lt=Yamatohime-no-Mikoto}} (やまとひめのみこと)

(keizer)|no|Keiko (keiser)|pl|Keikō|pt|Imperador Keikō|ru|Император Кэйко|sh|Car Keikō|simple|Emperor Keikō|sl|Cesar Kejko|sv|Keiko (kejsare)|th|จักรพรรดิเคโก|tl|Emperador Keikō|tr|Keikō (imparator)|uk|Імператор Кейко|uz|Imperator Keikō|vi|Thiên hoàng Keikō|yo|Emperor Keikō|zh|景行天皇|zh_min_nan|Keikô Thian-hông|zh_yue|景行天皇|qid=Q329723}} (the 12th emperor)'s 40th year includes the story that {{ill|Kuma District, Kumamoto|ceb|Kuma-gun|fr|District de Kuma|it|Distretto di Kuma|ja|球磨郡|ko|구마군|lt|Kumos apskritis|pl|Powiat Kuma|zh|球磨郡|qid=Q1132476|lt=Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto}} encountered a violent storm at Hashirimizu Sea (the {{ill|Uraga Channel|Q723431|qid=Q723431}}) during his eastern expedition, but was able to land safely in Kazusa through the self-sacrifice of his consort {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ototachibana-hime}}. Shrine tradition says that at that time Ototachibana-hime prayed to the deity of {{ill|Tatsuta Taisha|Q246455|qid=Q246455}} in {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}}, vowing to enshrine a wind-calming god if safe passage to Kazusa were granted; in accordance with her last wish, Yamato Takeru enshrined Shinatsuhiko-no-Mikoto here.

Shrine tradition also states that in the 57th year of Emperor Keiko, after Yamato Takeru's death,<ref>[http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=2052 Shimaana Shrine] (Jinja no Hiroba).</ref> Emperor Keiko, father of Yamato Takeru, visited places associated with Yamato Takeru's eastern campaign and jointly enshrined the divine spirits of Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto and Yamatohime-no-Mikoto at this shrine.

=== Overview ===
In the {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168|lt=official national histories}}, it is recorded that in {{ill|Gangyō|Q747451|qid=Q747451}} 1 ({{ill|877|Q23905|qid=Q23905}}), "Shimaana-no-kami" was granted the rank of junior fifth rank, lower grade, merit grade five ({{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}}).

In the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}}'' "{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Register of Shrines}}" compiled in {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Encho}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), it appears in {{ill|Kazusa Province|Q1055394|qid=Q1055394}}, {{ill|Unakami district|ja|海上郡 (上総国)|qid=Q11558726|lt=Unakami District}} as "Shimaana Jinja," and is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}. Among place names in the mid-Heian ''{{ill|Wamyō Ruijushō|Q2702542|qid=Q2702542|lt=Wamyōshō}}'', this area is identified with "Shimaano-go, Unakami District"{{Sfn|Anesaki Shrine and Shimaana Shrine (Kami-gami)|1984}}.

The shrine once had close ties with the likewise Shikinaisha {{ill|Anesaki Shrine|ja|姉埼神社|sv|Anesaki-jinja|qid=Q11447235}}, and it is said the sacred palanquin traveled between the two shrines.

After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, in {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}) it was listed as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}, and in Meiji 12 ({{ill|1879|Q7783|qid=Q7783}}) it was promoted to {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=kensha|qid=Q90139226}} under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}.

=== Ranks granted to the deity ===
* {{ill|Gangyō|Q747451|qid=Q747451}} 1 ({{ill|877|Q23905|qid=Q23905}}), 5th month 17th day: promoted from junior fifth rank upper, merit grade five, to senior fifth rank lower, merit grade five (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}'') - recorded as "Shimaana-no-kami".
* Gangyo 8 ({{ill|884|Q23895|qid=Q23895}}), 7th month 15th day: promoted from senior fifth rank lower, merit grade five, to senior fifth rank upper, merit grade five (''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'') - recorded as "Shimaana-no-kami".

There are several other small shrines in the precinct.

=== Related site ===
[[File:Shimaana-jinja, former place.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Former shrine site}}{{small|The current shrine site is farther in beyond the {{ill|Uchibō Line|Q1142964|qid=Q1142964}} tracks.}}]]
* Former shrine site
*: Located about 200 meters north of the present site, on the far side of the railway line. It is traditionally transmitted as the former seat of Shimaana Shrine, and is said to have once covered a considerable area. Formerly there was a deep cave in the woods, and because a clear wind was said to always blow from it, it was considered an action place of Shinatsuhiko-no-Mikoto, the wind deity; the shrine name "Shimaana" is also said to derive from this{{Sfn|Anesaki Shrine and Shimaana Shrine (Kami-gami)|1984}}. Although no cave is confirmed today and the tradition cannot be verified, it has been suggested that the tradition may refer to the stone chamber of an ancient tumulus{{Sfn|Anesaki Shrine and Shimaana Shrine (Kami-gami)|1984}}.
